notes: Handwritten Carr 5-5-PG. Cover 'Name of Office' reads 'Cache County Council' with 'Office District' = 'Northeast District' — AGREES with the chunk file's office=County Council. 'Full Name of Candidate' reads 'Val K. Potter' vs the chunk file's 'Val Potter' (the form carries the middle initial). County office, in scope. Cover date written out 'October 21, 2010'; clerk RCVD stamp '21 OCT 2010 PM12:10' — matches the chunk file's 2010-10-21. 3-page PDF; the printed form's page-4 statute sheet was not scanned. ⚠ FLAG FOR A HUMAN — CONTRACT TENSION ON THE '1,000.-' NOTATION: every Form A amount on this filing is written in the bookkeeping no-cents form '1,000.- / 100.- / 5,000.-'. Core brief section 3(g) lists '2,250.-' among MALFORMED DECIMALS (blank + needs_review) but in the very next clause rules that 'a trailing dash after whole dollars (1000-) means no cents -> 1000.00, noted'. The two clauses conflict for a comma-grouped value. I applied the trailing-dash rule, because the document's own arithmetic is decisive and outranks notation (section 2): only the readings 1000/100/5000/1000/100 make the five rows total the 7,200. printed on the cover, and blanking them would have manufactured a false floor on a schedule that closes to the cent. Every affected row carries needs_review:1 and the verbatim string in its note, so the decision is reversible. This is a good CALIBRATION-SPECIMEN CANDIDATE for disambiguating the two clauses. Second notation point: several amounts use a DECIMAL COMMA ('195,03', '51,79') — transcribed verbatim per the currency rule. ⚠ The Form A address column on this filing PRINTS NO STATE (city + ZIP only), so donor_state is honestly BLANK on all five rows rather than inferred as UT. Privacy: full street addresses and ZIPs in the Form A column, and the candidate's home address and two phone numbers on the cover, were discarded at read time.
